prerequisites: Knowledge of mathematics (especially Linear Algebra, Analysis) as acquired in introductory modules.

learning_outcomes.text: Graduates have basic knowledge in the field of weak AI. They are able to perform simple AI development tasks under guidance, including using HPC computing.
Students are enabled and guided to independently deepen their knowledge and practical competencies in selected topics (e.g., special algorithms).
Students can evaluate and critically reflect on the applicability of AI development approaches and algorithms.
Students can transfer learned content and concepts to new tasks.
Graduates are able to present their work results orally and in writing in a clearly structured form and discuss them with team members, "virtual" clients, and subject matter experts.

syllabus_topics: Machine Learning as a subfield of AI
Further current learning methods, e.g., Transformer / generative AI, Attention Networks, Generative Adversarial Networks
AI development and AI development environments
Selected topics in AI, e.g., Recommender systems, Process mining, Image understanding, Time series analysis, Web mining, Distributed learning methods
Introduction to the use of High-Performance Computing clusters
assessment_rules: The selection of graded and ungraded examination types from the given options is at the discretion of the respective lecturer, who adheres to the valid study regulations. For the graded examination, an oral exam or a written assignment (approx. 15 pages with an accompanying 10-minute presentation) is possible. For the ungraded examination, experimental work (approx. 5 experiments in total) or regular participation (at least 80% attendance) is required.
